In this system, the position of a point P is described by its distance from origin, O, and the amount of counterclockwise turn from a baseline OA to OP. Thus, the coordinates of P are (5, 340°).

A. Mark the points B (3, 30°) and C (4, 120°) on the graph above.
B. Draw the angle BOC. What is the measure of angle BOC?

Angle BOC = ____°

Figure, described in words:
A circular polar coordinate grid centered at an origin O, formed by 6 concentric circles. A horizontal baseline ray extends right from O, labeled A at its end, with the 6 concentric circles labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 along this ray. Radial line segments extend from O every 10° around the full circle, labeled on the outer rim counterclockwise from 0° at ray OA through 10°, 20°, 30°, up to 350°. A point labeled P is plotted on the 5th circle along the 340° radial line.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Mark B on the 3rd circle at 30° and C on the 4th circle at 120°. Draw rays OB and OC. Since 120° − 30° = 90°, angle BOC = 90°.
